content: 1. Ibuprofen injection, marketed under the brand name Caldolor®, is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) approved by the FDA for the treatment of fever, headache, migraine, osteoarthritis, pain, primary dysmenorrhea, and rheumatoid arthritis. It is administered intravenously. 2. The drug carries a Black Box Warning due to risks of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation, as well as other severe adverse effects. 3. Common side effects include hypotension, rash, hypernatremia, flatulence, heartburn, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and urinary retention. 4. For pain management in adults, the recommended dose is 400–800 mg intravenously every 6 hours as needed, with an infusion time of no less than 30 minutes. For fever reduction, the dose is 400 mg intravenously initially, followed by 400 mg every 4–6 hours or 100–200 mg every 4 hours as needed. 5. The total daily dose of ibuprofen should not exceed 3200 mg. Patients must be well-hydrated before administration to reduce the risk of renal adverse effects. 6. Caldolor must be diluted before intravenous infusion to a final concentration of 4 mg/mL or less. Suitable diluents include 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection (normal saline), 5% Dextrose Injection (D5W), or Lactated Ringer’s Solution. 7. The diluted solution is stable for up to 24 hours at room temperature (20–25°C) and under normal room lighting. The solution should be visually inspected for particulate matter or discoloration before use, and any compromised solution should be discarded. 8. Caldolor is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to ibuprofen, those with a history of asthma or allergic reactions to NSAIDs, and in the perioperative setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. 9. NSAIDs, including ibuprofen, are associated with an increased risk of serious cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction and stroke, particularly in patients with pre-existing cardiovascular disease or risk factors. The lowest effective dose should be used for the shortest duration possible. 10. Gastrointestinal risks include serious adverse events such as bleeding, ulceration, and perforation, which can occur at any time during therapy, even without warning symptoms. Patients with a history of peptic ulcer disease or GI bleeding are at significantly higher risk. 11. Hepatic effects may include elevations in liver enzymes (ALT, AST) and, in rare cases, severe reactions such as fulminant hepatitis, liver necrosis, or hepatic failure. Patients with signs of liver dysfunction should discontinue the drug and undergo evaluation. 12. Ibuprofen can cause or worsen hypertension and may reduce the efficacy of antihypertensive medications such as ACE inhibitors, thiazides, and loop diuretics. 13. Fluid retention and edema have been observed in some patients taking NSAIDs. Caution is advised in patients with heart failure or fluid retention. 14. Renal toxicity, including renal papillary necrosis, has been reported with long-term NSAID use. Patients with impaired renal function, heart failure, liver dysfunction, or those taking diuretics or ACE inhibitors are at higher risk. 15. Serious skin reactions, including Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), have been reported. Patients should discontinue the drug at the first sign of rash or hypersensitivity. 16. It is classified as Pregnancy Category D after 30 weeks. 17. The safety and efficacy of Caldolor in pediatric patients under 17 years of age have not been established. 18. Elderly patients are at increased risk for serious gastrointestinal adverse events and should be started on the lowest effective dose. 19. Ibuprofen may interact with other drugs, including aspirin, anticoagulants, ACE inhibitors, diuretics, lithium, and methotrexate, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects or reducing the efficacy of these medications. 20. In cases of overdose, symptoms may include abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, drowsiness, and dizziness. There is no specific antidote for ibuprofen overdose, and treatment is supportive. 21. Ibuprofen exerts its effects by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis, which contributes to its anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyretic properties. 22. Caldolor is supplied as an 800 mg/8 mL (100 mg/mL) single-dose vial and should be stored at controlled room temperature (20–25°C).
